senses.sense_definition: A dog kept to guard property and give warning of intruders.

examples.text: The farm is protected by a fierce <w>watchdog</w> that barks at any stranger who approaches.
They decided to get a trained <w>watchdog</w> to secure the warehouse at night.

senses.sense_definition: A person, committee, or organization that monitors the activities of companies or public institutions to ensure they act legally and ethically.

examples.text: The independent consumer <w>watchdog</w> has launched an investigation into the company's misleading advertising practices.
As an official government <w>watchdog</w>, the agency reports directly to parliament about corruption.

senses.sense_definition: A hardware or software mechanism that automatically resets or takes corrective action if a computer system malfunctions.

examples.text: If the main processor hangs unexpectedly, the internal <w>watchdog</w> will reboot the entire system.
The firmware regularly signals the <w>watchdog</w> to prevent an accidental reboot during normal operations.

senses.sense_definition: To monitor and protect against illegal or unethical activities, guarding public or organizational interests.

examples.text: Several civic groups have banded together to <w>watchdog</w> local election campaigns and ensure fairness.
The committee is tasked to <w>watchdog</w> how taxpayer funds are distributed across the districts.

senses.sense_definition: To reset or service a watchdog timer regularly to indicate normal functioning.

examples.text: The microcontroller must properly <w>watchdog</w> the circuit within every processing cycle to avoid a restart.
If the main loop fails to <w>watchdog</w> the board, a hardware interrupt is triggered immediately.
